Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000283": As of 2025-03-31, the auth gateway is a Team Boreal service.  (about: Team Boreal, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000271": As of 2025-03-28, the webhooks service lives with Team Atlas.  (about: Team Atlas, webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000267": As of 2025-03-28, the pager for the webhooks service rings Team Atlas instead of Team Boreal.  (about: Team Atlas, Team Boreal, webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000237" [constraint]: The webhooks service only ships on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.  (about: webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000232": The ledger relies on the auth gateway for service tokens, so if the auth gateway is down, the ledger service is down.  (about: ledger, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000225": As of 2025-03-17, the billing service lives with Team Boreal.  (about: Team Boreal, billing service)
- memory_id "1000222": Tomasz Nowak wrote the billing-api handover doc for Marcus on 2025-03-17.  (about: Tomasz Nowak, Marcus)
- memory_id "1000208": The billing service depends on the ledger for invoice postings.  (about: ledger, billing service)
- memory_id "1000196": On 2025-02-27, Team Boreal noticed the feature-flags service's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners.  (about: Team Boreal, feature-flags service)
- memory_id "1000193": As of the 2025-02-27 on-call swap, Marcus carries the Team Boreal on-call phone until the next rotation.  (about: Team Boreal, Marcus)
- memory_id "1000186" [constraint]: The event bus deploys on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.  (about: event bus)
- memory_id "1000156": During INC-2025-004, a stuck offset went unnoticed for 40 minutes.  (about: INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000154": The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart.  (about: INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000117": The webhooks service depends on the event bus for outbound events.  (about: event bus, webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000114": The notifier depends on the event bus for delivery events.  (about: event bus, notifier)
- memory_id "1000082": Lena takes the first Boreal on-call shift of the year.  (about: Team Boreal, Lena)
- memory_id "1000064": The notifier lives with Team Boreal.  (about: Team Boreal, notifier)
- memory_id "1000058": The event bus is owned by Team Boreal.  (about: Team Boreal, event bus)
- memory_id "1000042": The feature-flags service lives with Team Atlas.  (about: Team Atlas, feature-flags service)
- memory_id "1000011": As of January 2025, the Boreal team consists of Lena and Marcus.  (about: Team Boreal, Lena, Marcus)
Existing entity names: Team Boreal, auth gateway, Team Atlas, webhooks service, ledger, billing service, Tomasz Nowak, Marcus, feature-flags service, event bus, INC-2025-004, notifier, Lena

The note does state a relationship (ownership, "remains" = still holds). Adding a relation that already exists... The instructions say "Add one for each relationship the note states." The note states the event bus is a Boreal service, i.e., owned/maintained by Team Boreal. Adding relation Team Boreal owns event bus could be idempotent. But since it already exists implicitly, duplicating is harmless in graph terms. Hmm.

I think a conservative, clean patch: just the alias, or empty. Given the fact already exists and relations likely derived, I'll go with alias only. Actually, maybe include the relation too since notes establishing relationships should be added. "remains" implies it already existed, and fact 1000058 exists. Redundant. I'll keep it minimal: alias only.

The pattern in memory shows dated facts like "As of 2025-03-31, the auth gateway is a Team Boreal service." (memory 1000283). The note is similar in style. But the event bus ownership fact already exists without date; adding a dated reconfirmation duplicates. I'll skip.
